purpose: Pre-change golden weights for LogisticRegression.fit. Captured from the build at the head of master before the resume work landed, so that giving fit its two optional start parameters could be shown to leave a fresh run untouched. A fresh run of this configuration must still produce these values afterwards, bit for bit.

dataset.generator: MINSTD (Lehmer): s = (s * 48271) % 2147483647, starting from seed; each draw is (s - 1) / 2147483646. Every intermediate stays under 2^53, so the sequence is exact and portable across JS engines.
dataset.cellRule: draw < 0.4 ? 1 : 0, taken column by column within each row
dataset.classRule: one further draw per row, after its columns: draw < 0.5 ? 1 : 0, appended as the last element
dataset.note: LogisticRegression.fit reads the last element of each row as the class and sets dim to row length, so theta has columns + 1 entries: the intercept followed by one weight per column.

howToDriveIt: trace: true with a stepModeCallback that immediately calls next(i + 1). That configuration, and only that one, runs the whole fit synchronously, so the test needs no waiting.

determinismCheck.runnerNote: Run the suite with `npx jest` (jest.config.js), which is what the package.json test script does. `react-scripts test` picks up a different config that does not load src/test/setupTest.ts, so every jest-dom matcher fails and five suites look broken when they are not. These values were captured under react-scripts and then re-verified under ts-jest with an exact toEqual on the full theta arrays, cost and constantWeightTerm.
